messages:
maria-support: Hey @kevin-mlsdk, incoming from a customer: Python SDK streaming iterator appears to stop yielding tokens mid-response after a network blip. They say this used to work in 0.7.3 and regressed on 0.8.x. Can you take a look?

sam-customer: repro steps I gave them: minimal async snippet below. It starts streaming fine, then after a simulated short TCP drop the iterator returns an empty string and then StopAsyncIteration with no exception. No error in logs on our side, just truncated output.

sam-customer: Code:
```python
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def run():
    client = AsyncClient(api_key=...)
    async for chunk in client.stream("generate", prompt="Tell me a story", max_tokens=200):
        print(repr(chunk))

# simulate network blip with tcptracer or unplug cable in the middle of streaming
```

sam-customer: Observed output: first ~30 tokens printed, then '\'\'\'' (empty string) printed once, then loop exits (StopAsyncIteration) — story incomplete.

maria-support: They attached an HTTP-level capture showing server sent further SSE events after reconnect, but the client never resumed consuming them. I asked for SDK version: they reported 0.8.1.

kevin-mlsdk: Thanks, grabbing logs. Couple quick Qs: do they use the AsyncClient with default transport (aiohttp) or custom transport? Any proxy/pool in between?

sam-customer: Default aiohttp on Mac. No proxy. Single-threaded event loop. We tried increasing timeouts, no change.

kevin-mlsdk: Ok. This sounds like the async iterator's state machine is finalizing early when it sees a ConnectionClosed but then a reconnect path writes leftover buffer to the socket. Historically the iterator would raise a RecoverableStreamError and allow app-level retry; in 0.8.x we changed the lower-level generator to swallow the recoverable state and just stop iteration — bug.

kevin-mlsdk: Can you share the raw SSE frames? If we have them we can confirm whether the client parsed a final 'event: done' or if it just hit EOF.

sam-customer: Pasting snippet of captured SSE frames (redacted):
```
event: token
data: {"text":"Once upon a time,\n"}

<network gap: 2s>

event: token
data: {"text":"there was a coder who..."}

event: done
data: {"reason":"complete"}

```

sam-customer: After the gap the server re-sent the frames; curl -N against the endpoint shows complete stream on their machine. Only the SDK iterator disagrees.

kevin-mlsdk: That matches a bug I remember seeing in the iterator wrapper: when the aiohttp stream reader returns an empty chunk (b'') during backpressure, our internal _stream_generator marks EOF and returns. If the transport layer later reconnects and yields frames, the generator has already returned (StopAsyncIteration) and the consumer can't see them. We need to treat empty-read as transient, not terminal, unless we received a proper 'done' event.

alex-infra: tagging @infra-oncall in case network middlebox (e.g., ALB idle timeout) is killing connections and causing reconnects. We should also check that reconnects are transparent to the client.

infra-oncall: Confirmed customer sits behind an ALB with 60s idle timeout. We have a keepalive path but the SDK should be resilient to short disconnects.

kevin-mlsdk: Priority: P1 for SDK regression. Short-term workaround for customers: use explicit resume token parameter and handle reconnection manually, or pin to 0.7.3 if feasible. We'll also ship a patch to 0.8.x that treats empty reads as transient for stream parsing.

sam-customer: Workaround note: we tried manual reconnect logic and resume_token, and that works but is ugly. Would appreciate a patch.

kevin-mlsdk: Repro I just ran locally: used the same snippet but injected a socket close/reopen. I can reproduce StopAsyncIteration after partial output. Attaching my local trace:
```
DEBUG redwood.stream: read_chunk -> b'{"text":"Once upon a time,'\n'\n'\n'
DEBUG redwood.stream: read_chunk -> b''  # <-- treated as EOF
DEBUG redwood.stream: generator -> returning (StopAsyncIteration)
# later
DEBUG redwood.transport: reconnect -> new session established
DEBUG redwood.transport: sse_parse -> got token frames but generator already finished
```

kevin-mlsdk: Proposed fix: change read loop to treat b'' as 'yield control and retry after small backoff' unless we have already seen an explicit 'done' event or an unrecoverable HTTP status. Also add metrics/logging for 'transient-empty-chunk' to help ops. I'll open a PR.

maria-support: Please include a clear rollback/pin instructions for customers who cannot upgrade immediately.

kevin-mlsdk: Will do. Also adding test harness: simulated network drop + server resend; assert that async iterator continues until explicit 'done' event and that intermediate empty reads don't produce StopAsyncIteration.

dev-bot: CI: PR #2345 opened by kevin-mlsdk — tests added for transient empty reads and resume semantics.

kevin-mlsdk: Patch builds locally. Plan to cut 0.8.2 hotfix with this fix + release notes: 'Fix: Python async streaming iterator prematurely ends on brief transport disconnects (0.8.1 regression)'. Will publish wheel and skip semver breaking changes.

sam-customer: Great, thanks. Any ETA?

kevin-mlsdk: Aiming for release within 24 hours. I'll post the exact wheel URL here when published. In the meantime, workaround summary: either pin redwood==0.7.3 or implement manual reconnect with resume_token, or switch to synchronous client which doesn't exhibit this bug.

maria-support: I'll relay to customer and mark ticket as 'engineering triaged'. Thanks @kevin-mlsdk.

sam-customer: follow-up — also saw this with long-running prompts where the iterator returned a single '\n' then stopped. Will test the 0.8.2 candidate when available and report back.

kevin-mlsdk: Thanks — please include logs if still failing. We'll keep this thread updated with the release artifact and changelog entries.

maria-support: Closing loop: once we publish 0.8.2, let's paste the pip install command, the wheel link, and a tiny migration note in the release message.

kevin-mlsdk: Will do.
